Tiny Little Office

What leaves your browser

Tiny Little Office keeps a document in its link. Opening one asks the site for its own files and nothing else. This page lists every other request the site can make: when it happens, what it carries, and what stops it. The Content-Security-Policy in public/_headers allows these places and no others, so a request not on this list is refused by the browser itself.

Every request the site can make

tinylittleoffice.com

The site’s own files: the page, the app file (every app, the English words, the icons, the emoji and the math), its stylesheet, an app’s templates when its list opens, a language when a page is in it, and the type (IBM Plex, a face when a page’s words need it), each fetched once and kept a year.

A document fetches nothing from any other site but a trip's map (OpenFreeMap's in the Trip Planner, OpenStreetMap's tiles under a trip drawn anywhere else), by the Map switch. A link in it is words that go somewhere when the reader follows them; nothing else in a document is drawn from another site's address.

Why each of these is asked directly

  • The map. The Trip Planner's map comes from OpenFreeMap only while it is on the screen (its style, its vector tiles, its sprites and its fonts; MapLibre draws them here, fetched with the first map, never part of the app file; OpenFreeMap is made for this, with no key and no limit, and asks for no referrer); place search only when a search is tapped. A trip drawn on a slide, a page, an outline's item, a card or in an export is drawn on OpenStreetMap's tiles, at the zoom that fits its places: only the tiles its box needs (a handful, never a whole zoom level), nothing fetched ahead. A picture made of it (a card, a PDF, a PNG, a PowerPoint) fetches those tiles again to write them into the picture. The home page's pictures of the templates are drawn without them, so a visitor who has not opened a trip tells OpenStreetMap nothing, and Map in the Trip Planner's bar, turned off, turns them off everywhere. They are asked directly, by the browser with its own name: OpenStreetMap's usage policies are written for the browser that shows the map asking them directly, and a cache of ours in between would be the heavy, anonymous use they ask people not to make; nothing keeps them but the browser's own cache. The site sends no referrer.
  • Short links. Only when a short link is made or opened; the service holds ciphertext it cannot read, whose key is in the short link's fragment, which browsers never send (tinier/tinier.ts).
  • A preview. Only when a person shares with a network from Share with "Show a preview of the first page" on: a picture of the first page, the title and the first words go to the site's own /card, and the link shared carries the card's id in its path (/c/<id>, before the "#"): the one page the site's Worker serves, the app's page with the card's tags, which the shell moves to the app's own address as it opens. The card is kept readable for a month, then forgotten (tinier/cards.ts); the document and its link are never sent.
  • Sharing to a service. Share's Bluesky, Mastodon, X and LinkedIn open that service's own compose box in a new tab, with the title and the link in it: no script of theirs runs here. The link is the document, so whoever reads the post can read it. "Any https address" there is the Mastodon server the person names.
  • Fonts and icons. Self-hosted, from the site itself: the type is IBM Plex (public/fonts/), each face fetched when a page's words need it, and the policy's font-src is 'self' alone; the icons and the emoji are in the site's own app file.
  • Offline. With Save in browser on, the site's service worker (/sw.js, from src/sw.ts) keeps the site's own files on the device: the eleven pages, the app file, its stylesheet, the manifest and icons and the Latin faces when it is installed, and each file a page fetches afterwards (an app's templates, a language, a face). It asks only the site, and only for its files; a page is asked of the network first, so a visit online is never stale. It never keeps a document (the document is after the "#", which never reaches it) nor a shared link's /c/<id> page. Turning Save in browser off unregisters it and deletes everything it kept; while it is off nothing registers.
  • Links. A link in a document that leaves the site opens only after the reader is shown where it goes and says Go (kit/ui/link-guard.ts), in a new tab with no referrer.

Nothing else

No analytics, no error reporting, no fonts or scripts from a CDN, no tag manager, no fetch the person did not cause. test/network.test.ts reads the source (src/ and the shortener in tinier/) and fails on any host that is not on this page, and on any analytics, error-reporting, font-CDN or tag-manager host anywhere in the site.

How this page is kept true

It is written from src/kit/core/network.ts, the one list of every host, by scripts/network-doc.ts (npm run docs:network, which npm run build runs first); a test fails when the committed page is not what the list says. Every module that asks the web takes its host from that list, so a new host cannot be reached without appearing here. The policy's connect-src and img-src are written from the same list (scripts/headers.ts), and test/csp.test.ts holds each host to the directive the list names and nothing else; the policy has no frame-src or media-src of its own, so no frame, film or sound comes from another site.

Written from src/kit/core/network.ts; the same page is docs/network.md in the repository.
